An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. 6	```json

8	  "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" } ] }
9	```
10	- Exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`; `nextId` a positive safe integer.
11	- Each booking has exactly the keys id, room, title, date, start, end; id a positive

13	  start/end valid by the spec rules; start < end; no two same-room same-date overlaps.
14	- Anything else (empty file, invalid JSON, extra keys, ...) -> stderr
15	  `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` and exit 1. ENOENT -> `{nextId:1,bookings:[]}`.
16	- Written with `JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) + "\n"` directly to the path (no temp
17	  file, no mkdir), only on successful POST/DELETE, before the reply.
18	- Test tip: a fresh empty state on disk is `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}`.
19	
20	## Page files
21	- `GET /` -> `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`),
22	  `GET /app.js` -> `public/app.js` (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`).
23	- Located via `new URL('./public/...', import.meta.url)` (server.mjs folder, not cwd).
24	- Read from disk on every request (no cache); a read failure -> 500 `internal error` JSON.
25	
26	## Concurrency
27	- Every request's body is read fully first (only the first 10000 bytes are kept; all
28	  bytes are counted for 413), then routing + handling run through one FIFO queue, so
29	  state changes and saves are strictly serialised. A failed save leaves memory unchanged.
30	
31	## stdout / stderr
32	- stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n`. Bad PORT / bind error: one
33	  stderr line, exit code 1.

content.text:
**server.mjs passes with a score of 9/10 and package.json is fine.** The Bash smoke test (startup errors, port in use, 413/415 order, BOM body, save failure) was denied, so this grade comes from reading the code only. Nothing was run.

I checked both files against the spec and the design note and found no spec errors:
- **Startup:** it checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then listens. Only the listen line goes to stdout. `ENOENT` means no bookings yet; any other read error or a file in the wrong layout gives `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` and exit 1. Relative paths resolve against the working directory.
- **Routing:**
  - Paths are compared byte for byte on the raw `req.url`, split at the first `?`.
  - The booking-item rule (non-empty rest with no `/`) is correct, and `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` fall through to 404 `not found`.
  - 405 covers HEAD and OPTIONS, and `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405.
  - `?date` with no `=` counts as present, the first value wins when repeated, and an empty value gets 400.
- **Body handling:** every request's body is read in full before any reply. All received bytes are counted for 413, but at most 10000 are kept. The 415 check runs before 413. The media type is split at the first `;`, only spaces and tabs are trimmed, and case is ignored. The body is decoded with `toString('utf8')`, so a leading BOM makes it invalid JSON.
- **Booking rules:**
  - Rules 4 to 10 run in spec order.
  - Only the title is trimmed, and its length is checked after trimming.
  - February has 29 days in years divisible by 4, within 2000 to 2099.
  - Overlap uses strict `<` on both sides, and the 409 names the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
  - DELETE ids must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`.
- **Saving:** `store.commit` writes the file before it updates memory, so a failed save leaves state and `nextId` unchanged and replies 500. One FIFO queue handles routing and saves, so concurrent requests are processed one at a time. Page files are found relative to `server.mjs`.
- **package.json:** `"type": "module"`, `start` runs `node server.mjs`, `test` runs `node --test`, and there are no dependencies.

Small issues:
- **Line 331:** the bad-`PORT` message includes the raw value. A `PORT` containing a newline would write more than the one stderr line the spec allows.
- **Lines 310-313:** the error behind a 500 is thrown away without any record. The client reply is correct, but nothing shows why it failed.
- **Line 338:** the `'error'` handler is attached with `once`. It is only meant for bind failures, and an unrelated server error after that would have no handler.
- **Unverified:** after a failed bind, `fail` only sets `process.exitCode` and does not exit. The process should still exit with code 1 because nothing else keeps it alive, but I could not confirm that without running it.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — clear layers (validation, data file, HTTP helpers, rules, routing, queue/store, main); state replaced not mutated; nesting shallow
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent; only one-letter `b` lambdas and the terse `only`/`MSG`
duplication: 9 — validators reused across POST rules and data-file checks; no copy-paste
size: 10 — 345 lines, all functions well under 50 lines
errors: 8 — boundaries validated, OS errors split by err.code, save rollback correct; bad-PORT line can break across lines, and the cause of a 500 is thrown away without any record
tests: n/a — written by the testing section
security: 9 — no secrets, no path traversal (fixed page map), body memory capped at 10000 bytes
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs; the one comment explains the queue
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:331 do not put the raw PORT value in the message (or use JSON.stringify(process.env.PORT)) so stderr is always exactly one line
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:310 bind the caught error and write a one-line stderr note (e.g. `internal error: ${error.code ?? error.name}`) so the cause of a 500 is not lost; stdout must stay untouched
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs:338 after listening succeeds, remove the bind-error handler or replace it with a runtime one, so a later server 'error' is not mislabelled as a listen failure (optional)
